Significant events to be reported: Signing of a EUR 500,000,000 Bridge Facility Agreement

Electrica informs its shareholders and investors that on 26 November 2026 it signed, as borrower, a bridge facility agreement (the "Facility Agreement") for up to EUR 500,000,000, with Erste Group Bank AG, acting as Bookrunner and Mandated Lead Arranger, Documentation Agent and Original Lender, Banca Transilvania S.A. and ING Bank N.V. Amsterdam, Bucharest Branch as Original Lenders and Banca Comercială Română S.A. as Agent.

The Facility Agreement was concluded under Resolution no. 1/2026 of Electrica's Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders („EGMS”) of 29 April 2026. The resolution approved "the contracting by Societatea Energetică Electrica S.A. of one or more secured / unsecured loans in a total amount of up to EUR 1,000,000,000 (of a "bridge" type compared to the bonds to be issued by the Company), based on a credit agreement/credit agreements (generically referred to as the "Credit Agreement") concluded with one or more financial institutions (the "Financing Parties"), having a repayment term of up to maximum 24 months from the disbursement date of each relevant loan.". More details can be found in the Resolution available here, items 20 and 21.

The facility serves as bridge financing ahead of the bonds to be issued under the EUR 1,000,000,000 Euro Medium Term Note Programme („EMTN Programme”). The EMTN Programme was approved by the EGMS through the same Resolution of 29 April 2026 (items 18 and 19).  Its base prospectus was approved by the Luxembourg Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier on 29 October 2026. More details about the EMTN can be found here.

The amounts borrowed under the Facility Agreement are for financing Electrica’s general corporate purposes in respect of which proceeds are permitted to be applied in accordance with the EMTN Programme, excluding the payment of dividends.

Statement by Mr. Alexandru Chirita, CEO: "To our partners Erste Group Bank, Banca Transilvania, ING Bank, and Banca Comercială Romanian, as well to our colleagues at Electrica, who took the transaction from shareholder approval to signing, I extend my appreciation – thank you! We arrived here step by step: In April 2026, shareholders approved the bond Programme and the bridge financing. In September, Fitch reconfirmed the BBB- rating, with a stable outlook. In October, the base prospectus of the EMTN Programme was approved and the program was established.

Optimizing and reducing costs, as well as ensuring liquidity in advance for investment projects, are part of our management strategy. We will continue as follows: financing contracted in advance, at the lowest possible costs, for a company that invests in networks, production, and storage, but especially in people, while also bringing added value to its investors."

data.title: Black Friday sales can rise while Kogan's Christmas profit falls
data.description:
Black Friday turnover is a poor substitute for retail profit. The rush for discounts points to Christmas spending being pulled forward, with Kogan’s margins caught in the contest.

Inflation meets the sales

Annual consumer price inflation rose to 4.9% in October, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said. The Reserve Bank had already raised its cash rate target to 4.85% on 3 November, citing inflation and pressure on domestic capacity. That is the household squeeze behind this year’s sales.

Against it, the Australian Retail Council and Roy Morgan forecast Black Friday spending growth of 5.5%. They estimate 5.8 million Australians intend to shop, fewer than last year, while planned spending per shopper has risen. Australia Post has added 3,500 delivery workers, and its network operations executive Shane Plant says parcel volumes are already ahead of the same time last year.

Discounts bring Christmas forward

Shoppers’ reasons for participating matter as much as the headline forecast. The Australian Retail Council and Roy Morgan found that low prices and saving on Christmas gifts had become more common motivations than a year earlier. A household buying presents on sale now has less reason to buy them at full price later.

Retailers have also stretched the event. Amazon Australia began its Black Friday promotion well before the sales weekend and runs it through the end of November. That puts pressure on rivals to promote for longer, increasing the sales exposed to reduced prices.

We think this is a bargain hunt, not evidence that higher interest rates have lost their bite. The decisive measure is gross profit across November and December: sales revenue left after the cost of goods. A bigger November can still leave Kogan with less profit from Christmas trading.

Kogan’s profit test

Kogan.com (ASX: KGN) has a direct stake in the online rush. It has told the market that its peak retail period covers Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Christmas and Boxing Day, and that the period contributed to accelerated half-year growth. The sales event is part of a longer trading season, not a standalone earnings result.

Kogan stands to gain sales from shoppers chasing value online. The squeeze comes if it needs deeper discounts to win those orders, or if purchases made in November displace full-price December sales. Higher revenue alongside weaker gross profit would be an expensive victory. Growth in both across the combined period would make a stronger case that the promotion brought in profitable demand.

ASX small caps exposed

CompanyExposureMarket cap

Ingenia Communities Stapled Unt Real Estate: Property valuations and borrowing costs move with interest rates$1.81bn
Judo Capital Holdings Banks: Net interest margins and loan demand move with the cash rate$1.81bn
Hmc Capital Diversified Financials: Lending, funding costs and investor flows move with rates$1.80bn
Growthpoint Pro Aus Reit Stapled Unt Real Estate: Property valuations and borrowing costs move with interest rates$1.77bn
Bapcor Limited Retailing: Promotional sales and consumer demand influence retailer revenue and margins$1.75bn

Screened by Small Caps from company project and sector data; market caps are indicative.

Shoppers still have capacity

The bullish reading is that households are spending despite inflation and higher borrowing costs. The Australian Retail Council and Roy Morgan’s forecast points to growth in total sales even with fewer intended participants. Plant’s account of parcel volumes adds evidence of activity before the weekend.

Monash University also found more shoppers planned to buy during Black Friday than on Boxing Day. Believers in the spending story can argue that retailers are following demand to the event customers prefer. We still favour the margin test: shifting purchases to a cheaper sales window is valuable to households, yet it leaves retailers needing more volume to protect profit.

The Christmas profit count

From 27 November, actual Black Friday trading is the first check on the Australian Retail Council and Roy Morgan’s 5.5% growth forecast. Strong turnover would support the spending case; a weaker result would leave the forecast looking optimistic.

Through Christmas and Boxing Day, the more revealing comparison is combined November and December gross profit. Growth would support the argument that the sales created profitable demand. Falling gross profit alongside rising sales would support our view that discounts and earlier purchases are taking the edge off the rush.

When Kogan next reports its half-year results, revenue and gross profit across the peak season provide the company-level check. Growth in both would challenge our margin concern; higher sales with weaker gross profit would reinforce it.

data.title: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description:
Key points:
  • State Council flags expanded role for "national team"
  • CSI300 index leaps 4.2%, Shanghai Composite up 3.7%
  • Semiconductor index notches record gains
  • Investors say it's a short-term support

By Summer Zhen and Rae Wee

Chinese stocks roared up from 17-month lows on Friday, notching their largest gains in more than two years after Beijing flagged a bigger role for state-backed investors in a move to stabilise a struggling market.

The move could put a floor under prices, which have been sliding relentlessly since July on worries about weak consumer demand, the prolonged property downturn and the risk that trade tensions threaten the economy's one bright spot in exports.

A bigger role for the "national team" of state investors is also the latest sign of authorities stepping into markets to shore up bets on the AI infrastructure buildout.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended 3.7% up and the blue-chip CSI300 index was 4.2% higher at the close, both notching their biggest daily gains since October 2024 when China rolled out massive stimulus to revive the market.

China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 15% for its biggest one-day jump in two years, while a sub-index tracking semiconductors (.CSI950125) soared 19%, marking its biggest single-day gain on record.

The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 2.1% while the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped more than 6%.

"It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong.

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."

CHEERS FOR NATIONAL TEAM

China's "national team" is the name traders have given to a loose collection of state investors who tend to be buyers at times of stress and a source of near-constant speculation about their habits and intentions.

Investors took it as a strong signal of support when state media Xinhua reported that Central Huijin, a lead player in the team, would enhance its roleas a quasi-stabilisation fund after a meeting of China's cabinet — the State Council.

"Giving this message from the very top level ... it is an attempt to re-instill some confidence, stabilise liquidity and stabilise the trajectory of the market," said Winnie Wu, head of Asia equity strategy and co-head of China equity research at BofA Global Research in Hong Kong.

"There's probably this awareness that AI is strategically, economically and financially very important, and they don't want to see a big fallout in this space."

The Chinese yuan also gained against the dollar and is near its firmest level for four years.

The move also followed relaxations to margin lending rules, aimed at reducing selling pressure in the market, and on Friday Xinhua Finance separately reported that regulators would tighten rules on share sales by controlling shareholders of listed companies and guard against listings by firms that inflate earnings.

Investors will have the weekend to consider whether Beijing's support changes a deep-seated wariness about China's equity markets, where before the news the tech-heavy STAR 50 and ChiNext indexes had slumped roughly 50% since July.

"There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank.

"I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals... A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom."

data.title: Rupee rally takes a hit as AI trade revival dents shares, currency sees weekly dip
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

The Indian rupee's recent rally faltered on Friday as a drop in local equities amid renewed interest in AI trades threatened to slow the foreign inflows that have supported the currency.

The rupee opened marginally lower at 92.52 against the US dollar and weakened to 92.9925 before closing 0.6% lower at 92.99, taking its weekly losses to 0.3%. It had jumped 1.7% last week.

Foreign investors have bought about $16 billion of Indian equities in November, reversing a significant portion of the outflows recorded in the first 10 months of the year.

The inflows have helped the rupee outperform most of its Asian peers despite the dollar index hovering near a two-year high. Renewed demand for AI-heavy markets, however, could threaten that support.

Rising oil prices added to the pressure, with Brent crude climbing above $96.50 a barrel in Asian trade on supply concerns, renewing worries over India's rising import bill.

Dhaval Shah, founder and managing director of De-Risk Forex Consultancy, said "the recent upmove in oil prices due to geopolitical concerns has the rupee to pause its rally."

He pegged resistance for the dollar/rupee pair at 92.90-93.30, with a downside target of around 91.30.

Attention now turns to the Reserve Bank of India's December 4 policy decision.

The central bank is widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points, though some economists see scope for a larger hike, which could support the rupee.

In accordance with the notification obligations under Article 19 of the UK Market Abuse Regulation, Renishaw plc (the "Company") announces the following transactions relating to certain persons discharging managerial responsibilities of the Company (“PDMRs”) under the Renishaw plc Long-Term Incentive Plan (the “Plan”).

As mentioned in the Directors’ Remuneration Report of the Renishaw plc 2026 Annual Report (“DRR”), the number of Ordinary Shares subject to the Performance Share Awards has been calculated based on the average of the closing share price for an Ordinary Share for the three dealing days immediately preceding 21 October 2026 (£53.75).  This was the same share price as used to determine deferred annual bonus awards granted to William Lee and Kasim Hussain on 21 October 2026.

Details of the performance conditions that apply to the awards can be found in the DRR.  Subject to the performance conditions, the awards are scheduled to vest on 22 October 2029.  For William Lee and John Shipsey, as Executive Directors and consistent with our approved Directors’ Remuneration Policy, a two-year holding period applies post vesting, such that the awards will be released after the second anniversary of the vesting date. No payment was required for the grant of the Performance Share Awards.

data.title: The Hong Kong Institute of Directors Announces Winners of Director Excellence 2026 at the Institute's Annual Dinner
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 27, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - The Hong Kong Institute of Directors ('HKIoD') announced the winners of the HKIoD Awards for Director Excellence (the 'Awards') at its Annual Dinner held yesterday. The honours include the prestigious Directors of the Year Awards ('DYA'), Climate Governance Awards ('CGA'), and Social Impact Awards ('SIA').

The event began with an opening speech by Mr Richard Tsang, Chairman of the HKIoD. The guest of honour was Mr Christopher Hui, GBS, JP, Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury of the HKSAR.

After careful deliberation, the judging panel selected 16 winners who embody the theme of this year's awards: "Navigating Through Disruptive Forces in Challenging Times'. These outstanding individuals and boards exemplify the resilience required of modern boards to guide their organisations through rapid digital transformation, macroeconomic shifts, and evolving stakeholder expectations. Most importantly, their commitment to high standards of governance sets a benchmark for the entire business community in Hong Kong.

The Awardees of the HKIoD Awards*for Director Excellence 2026 are listed below:

*Three categories of Awards:

- 'DYA', acronym for 'Directors Of The Year Awards' (*In addition: recognition of Excellence in Board Diversity)

- 'CGA', acronym for 'Climate Governance Awards'

- 'SIA', acronym for 'Social Impact Awards

*In alphabetical order of names within category

Listed Companies Categories

Executive Directors

DYA Mr ZHANG Haipeng China State Construction International Holdings Limited

DYA Ms Tung Ming Yiu, Denise Town Ray Holdings Limited

Boards

DYA Board of China Resources Beverage (Holdings) Company Limited

DYA Board of Pin An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd.*In addition: recognition of Excellence in Board Diversity

Non-listed Companies Categories

Statutory/ Non-profit-distributing Organisations Categories

Boards

SIA Council of Hong Kong St. John Ambulance

DYA Hospital Authority Board *In addition: recognition of Excellence in Board Diversity

DYA & SIA Board of Mighty Oaks Foundation Limited *In addition: recognition of Excellence in Board Diversity

DYA Board of Governors, The Australian International School Foundation Limited *In addition: recognition of Excellence in Board Diversity

Richard Tsang, Chairman of HKIoD (front row, 6th from left), joins Council members and the 16 distinguished award recipients (back row) for a group photo.

About 'HKIoD Awards for Director Excellence'

The HKIoD Awards for Director Excellence is a project organised by The Hong Kong Institute of Directors ('HKIoD') and consists of three categories of Awards.

Directors Of The Year Awards was inaugurated in 2001 as the first ever such Awards organised in Asia. As directors are ultimately responsible for corporate governance and leading the company in prosperity and integrity, the objectives of the Awards are to recognise outstanding boards and directors and to promote good practices in corporate governance and director professionalism. The Awards have become an annual project of impact in the community organised by HKIoD together with over 100 Project Partners. To date, 303 Awardees have been recognised for their achievements in demonstrating exemplary high standards in corporate governance and director practice.

Inaugurated in 2024, Climate Governance Awards constitute the second category of HKIoD Awards with the objectives to recognise and inspire exemplary achievements in climate governance and to advocate climate action by directors. It is critical time now for directors to address the risks and opportunities of climate change in board agendas and their governance role.

Inaugurated in 2025, the Social Impact Awards, following the Climate Governance Awards, constitute the third category of HKIoD Awards. The Awards aim to recognise and inspire exemplary achievements in board governance leading to social sustainability and to advocate good practices in board governance contributing to social sustainability by directors. Four awardees have been acknowledged in the inaugural edition of the Awards.

Candidates are open to public nomination, with data processed in well-defined and stringent procedures, followed by interviews with independent consultants in utmost due diligence and finally selected by independent judges with high standards and fair judgment. Awards are presented by company categories, viz Listed Companies, Non-listed Companies and Statutory/Non-profit-distributing Organisations, and by capacities, viz Executive Directors, Non-Executive Directors and Boards.

About The Hong Kong Institute of Directors ('HKIoD')

The Hong Kong Institute of Directors ('HKIoD') is Hong Kong's premier body representing directors working together to advance corporate sustainability in creating long-term value for companies, their owners, stakeholders, humankind and Planet Earth through advocacy and standards-setting in corporate governance and director professionalism.

Led by Founder Chairman Dr The Hon Moses Cheng, HKIoD was founded in 1997. Throughout the years, HKIoD is honoured to have the Chief Executive of HKSAR as the Institute's Patron. Membership of HKIoD comprises of directors from diverse industries and corporate types and includes Executive Directors, Non-Executive Directors and Independent Non-Executive Directors. With multi-culturalism and international perspectives, HKIoD organises activities that cover director training, seminars and forums, collective director voice, guideline establishment, public education, Award Series for Director Excellence, assessment of Corporate Governance Scorecard for listed companies etc.

As a member body of the Global Network of Director Institutes ('GNDI'), HKIoD is committed to global collaboration in promoting good corporate governance and director professionalism. HKIoD is the appointed Host of the Hong Kong Chapter of Climate Governance Initiative, a global network that collaborates with the World Economic Forum in actively promoting directors' address of the risks and opportunities of climate change. For details please visit: http://www.hkiod.com | http://www.gndi.org | https://climate-governance.org/

data.title: Yomiuri: Japan Eyes 52% Capital Gains Tax on New Condo Flipping
data.description:
By Yui Orita

Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

The Japanese government and ruling parties are considering setting a 52% tax rate on capital gains if individuals sell new condominium units within one year of purchase without living there, as a measure to address persistently high prices of such properties, according to sources.

The envisaged taxation is aimed at curbing speculative transactions. Officials are finalizing details as they intend to include the measure in the ruling parties' tax system reform outline for fiscal 2027.

Under the current system, if the ownership period is five years or less as of Jan. 1 of the year in which a building or land is sold, a tax rate of about 40% applies to the capital gains. If the ownership period exceeds five years, the rate is about 20%.

The 52% tax rate is being envisaged in consideration of a system established in 1973 to impose heavier taxation on capital gains from land sales in response to rising land prices. The application of this system has been suspended since 1998.

The government and ruling parties intend to tighten regulations on transactions not only by individuals but also by corporations, by imposing a 10% tax on capital gains on top of their corporate tax liabilities for short-term sales of one year or less that do not involve residential use.

For verification of residential status, data such as from residential records is likely to be used.

Also regarding the real estate acquisition tax, which is paid a certain period after the acquisition of a home or land, discussions are underway for tougher taxation on short-term transactions.

----

This article is from The Yomiuri Shimbun. Neither Dow Jones Newswires, MarketWatch, Barron's nor The Wall Street Journal were involved in the creation of this content.

data.title: Chinese ride-hailing group Didi swings to third-quarter net loss
data.description:
Didi Global swung to a net loss in the third quarter, it said on Friday, citing losses in its international operations.

  • The company runs China's largest ride-hailing platform and has also expanded into Latin America

  • It posted a net loss of 789 million yuan ($118.57 million) for the July-September period, against a 1.46 billion yuan net profit a year earlier, on revenue up 12% at 65.7 billion yuan

  • The company said it would continue to actively develop its international business and autonomous driving initiatives

  • Didi has 60 million active users along with 2.5 million drivers and delivery partners in Brazil

($1 = 6.6543 Chinese yuan renminbi)

data.title: REG - EMH Treasury plc - S & P credit rating
data.description:
RNS Number : 9947E EMH Treasury plc 27 November 2026  

emh group reaffirms investment priorities following S&P outlook change

East Midlands-based housing and care provider emh group’s credit rating remains unchanged at A. S&P has revised the outlook on the rating from stable to negative.

In response to the revised outlook, emh is reaffirming its commitment to balancing financial resilience with continued investment in existing homes, new affordable housing and future services for customers.

Homes England recently confirmed emh as a Strategic Partner for the Government’s Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP), receiving £314 million to support the delivery of new affordable homes across the East Midlands. This funding will support emh, alongside its delivery partner, to build 2,495 homes over the next seven years, addressing priority housing need across the East Midlands.

Geoff Clarke, Executive Director of Finance at emh said:

“The revised outlook does not change our commitment to responsible decisions within our available resources. At emh, our priorities are clear: investing in and improving existing homes for today’s customers, building homes for future customers and equipping us to adapt as their needs change. We believe this is a balanced, long-term approach to investment in homes and services and financial resilience.”

The group will launch a new five-year corporate plan in 2027, setting out its priorities for that period. Its mission and values will continue to guide its investment priorities as it prepares for the new plan.
